audit.whatIsWrong: The chart read Skill/Yone/Yone/Skill/Skill/Yone/Yone. The already-audited chogath__yone mirror set the shared chart to Skill / Yone / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Skill / Yone, on the reasoning that Soul Unbound is still on 22 down to 16 seconds through those levels and cannot reset every trade.
audit.why: The two directions must state the same facts, and mirror-fix.js would overwrite any disagreement I introduced.
audit.corrected: win[2..4]/phases[2..4].side = Cho'Gath; win[5]/phases[5].side = Skill. Levels 1, 2 and Two+ items already matched. whys[2..5] and phases[2..5].why rewritten so the reasons follow the sides.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns for any of the three abilities the page is built around.
audit.why: Rupture is 6s from 950 range, Feral Scream is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s, Feast is 80/70/60s. Rupture coming back every 6 seconds is why 'trade around his Q' needs a number to mean anything.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, spikes[1] and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Feral Scream's silence is listed as a mistake heading ('Get silenced mid-combo') but its effect is never described, and the body text under it is boilerplate about a different ability. Feast is described as an 'execute' — it is a 175-range devour dealing true damage, which no amount of armour or MR reduces. spikes[1] also claims Soul Unbound gives you 'a body double and a guaranteed reset'; it returns you to your body's position, which is a rewind, not a reset, and spikes[3] tells you to 'W the Silence', which is not a thing Spirit Cleave does.
audit.why: Silenced you lose Mortal Steel, Spirit Cleave, Soul Unbound and Fate Sealed at once — that is the whole of your kit, and it is the reason his Q-into-W is lethal rather than annoying.
audit.corrected: Silence effect stated in the cooldown block and the don'ts; Feast described as true damage that resistances do not touch; the two false Yone descriptions removed.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Cho'Gath must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: His Q into Feral Scream chains a knock-up into a silence, and Soul Unbound is still on 22s. Hold the wave near you.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Rupture's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Soul Unbound is 19s here, so you can't reset out of every trade. Work around Rupture's 6s and bank only small leads.

edits.before: Fate Sealed sets up team knockups nothing can dodge. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Cho'Gath's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Feast is 80s of true damage that no resistance stops. Reassess every all-in at 6 — his ultimate changes the math.

edits.before: Blade of the Ruined King is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Rupture's cooldown.
edits.after: Blade of the Ruined King evens it — force fights on Rupture's cooldown once the item completes.

edits.before: Cho ults for the true-damage execute, but your R Fate Sealed and E Soul Unbound give you a body double and a guaranteed reset — dodge his Feast timing and you still walk out.
edits.after: Feast (R, 80s at rank 3) is true damage on a 175-range grab, so no armour or MR helps — stay out of melee at low HP. Soul Unbound returns you to your body, so start it from somewhere safe.

edits.before: Cho'Gath is a stat check you clear easily — R in, W the Silence, and shred the health stacks faster than he can Vorpal Spikes you.
edits.after: Cho'Gath is a stat check, but Feral Scream's silence still cuts your combo dead — open with Spirit Cleave from 700 range, then commit.

edits.before: You dictate the mid-game — your E lets you commit to a trade and reset out, so his only real threat (Q-W combo) rarely lands. Only the Skill window at 3 needs care, as a landed Rupture can start his combo.
edits.after: He dictates more of the mid-game than you'd like: Soul Unbound is 22s at rank 1, so you can't reset out of every trade. Rupture into Feral Scream silences your escape — space around the 6s Q and take the gaps.

edits.before: - Cho'Gath Rupture: matchup-defining — Telegraphed. Dodge with E. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Rupture: 6s, 950 range, delayed — sidestep the telegraph. - Feral Scream: 11s at rank 1, a cone silence that cuts your whole combo. - Feast: 80s at rank 3, true damage, so resistances do nothing.

edits.before: Telegraphed. Dodge with E. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: 6s, 950 range, and delayed — walk out of the telegraph, don't dash.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Feral Scream silences for seconds — no Q3, no W, no snap-back.

edits.before: E-ing in while his answer is up or overstaying the soul timer — the snap-back position is where Yones die.
edits.after: Every Feast stack is permanent max health, and the damage is true — armour will not save you from it.

notes: Chart follows the chogath__yone mirror rather than the packet, which marks all seven stages Yone against a 54.08% win rate — the two disagree and the mirror is what mirror-fix.js enforces. I did NOT touch phases[].rating: the mirror lists ratings 5,4,6,6,6,5,3 but those are written from Cho'Gath's side and I could not tell whether this page's ratings are meant to be the inverse, so flipping them blind risked shipping a worse number than the one already there. Kit-flag note: Cho'Gath's Rupture carries a 'grounding' flag, but Riot's own description says only that it pops enemies into the air, damages and slows. Per instructions I trusted the description and did not write grounding anywhere — if that flag is real it would deny Mortal Steel's dash and would change this matchup significantly.
